items.title: SAGE-QA: Semantic-Aware, Grounded Evaluation for Closed-Context Question Answering on SQuAD 2.0
items.summary_1line: Closed-context question answering (QA) requires a system to generate an answer strictly supported by a supplied passage, or to abstain when the passage lacks adequate evidence. SQuAD 2.0 is a widely used benchmark for this setting, scored by Exact Match (EM) i.e., character-level
items.editor_note: Turns the thread to evaluation: grounded, abstention-aware scoring in place of Exact Match.

editorial.tldr: The thread opened in late October with DocSkill, an arXiv paper applying skill-integrated agents to multilingual multi-hop document QA. LibriSpeech-Real-QA followed on Nov 4 with a benchmark for streaming speech QA, where models must answer before the full audio arrives.
editorial.whats_new: SAGE-QA (Nov 12) proposes semantic-aware, grounded scoring for SQuAD 2.0 closed-context QA, replacing character-level Exact Match with checks on whether answers are supported by the passage or correctly abstain.
editorial.why_it_matters: The thread has shifted from new QA methods to how QA is measured: if Exact Match misjudges grounded answers and abstentions, RAG eval suites built on it misreport faithfulness.
editorial.take_for_builders: If your QA or RAG evals score with Exact Match, spot-check a sample of grounded paraphrases and abstentions by hand before trusting the metric; treat all three papers as preprints until reproduced.

beats.headline: SAGE-QA challenges Exact Match scoring for grounded, abstention-aware QA
beats.summary: Moves the thread from methods to evaluation: scoring support from the passage and correct abstention on SQuAD 2.0.

open_questions: Do any of these methods report results that hold up outside their own benchmarks?
Will speech LLMs show measurable accuracy loss when answering before the full audio arrives?
How far do SQuAD 2.0 model rankings move when scored with SAGE-QA instead of Exact Match?
Is SAGE-QA's grounding check released as code that can be dropped into an existing RAG eval harness?
